chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jamilah and from Sindi, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the well-known woman (of the sect), should she be married to the Nāsib (one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt)? He said: No, because the Nāsib is a disbeliever. I said: Should she be married to a man who is neither Nāsib nor well-known (of the sect)? He said: The one who is neither is more beloved to me than the well-known one.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعفَر: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.العَارِفَة: Al-Arifah, a woman well-known for her sect or characteristics
key_terms.النّاصِب: Nāsib, one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a woman known for her sect to a Nāsib?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'Al-Arifah' (a woman known for her specific sect) is evaluated regarding inter-sect marriage, specifically with a Nāsib (enemy of the Ahl al-Bayt). The Imam establishes that while a Nāsib is a disbeliever and thus unsuitable, a man who is neither a Nāsib nor prominently identified with a rival sect is preferred over the 'well-known' sectarian woman, highlighting the importance of religious compatibility and avoiding prominent sectarian markers in marriage. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of prioritizing faith and avoiding those with enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt, even if they are not technically disbelievers in the strictest sense.
